status.en: 255 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, most of them in Lagos, Abuja and Plateau State.
status.nb: 255 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, flest i Lagos, Abuja og Plateau State.

summary.en: Gunmen have intensified attacks in Nigeria's Plateau region, killing a woman harvesting groundnuts and injuring two farmers, while Fulani attackers killed a farmer and wounded another in a separate raid. In eastern Nigeria, gunmen killed at least ten people and later reports indicate death tolls rising to forty in a village raid after Friday prayers. Bandits kidnapped two farmers in Kaduna and rescued 70 abducted persons were recovered by troops. The conflict produced 1,486 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Våpenbærende menn har økt angrepene i Nigerias Plateau-region, og drepte en kvinne som høstet jordnøtter og såret to bønder, mens Fulani-angripere drepte en bonde og såret en annen i et eget raid. I Øst-Nigeria drepte væpnede menn minst ti personer, og senere rapporter viser at dødstallet i et landsbyraid etter fredagsbønnene har steget til førti. Banditter kidnappet to bønder i Kaduna, og 70 bortførte personer ble reddet av tropper. Ifølge UCDP førte konflikten til 1 486 dødsfall i kamp i 2024.

background.title: Boko Haram insurgency
background.extract: The Boko Haram insurgency began in July 2009, when the militant Islamist and jihadist rebel group Boko Haram started an armed rebellion against the government of Nigeria. Boko Haram targets both Muslims and Christians. Attacks are often directed at individuals perceived as supporting the Nigerian government or Islamic State after the split between them, including civil servants, local defense groups, Muslim leaders who oppose the group and other rebels like al-Qaeda and Islamic State. Most attacks are not based on the religion of the victims.
